title: Admin worklet catalog and safe-runner primitives
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight catalog of small admin "worklets" (idempotent, parameterized runbook tasks) and a minimal 'safe-runner' runtime that enforces permission checks, dry-run mode, and automatic telemetry. Goal: give support and SREs a discoverable, auditable set of repeatable operations without granting shell access or ad-hoc scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog UI + API to list worklets with metadata (owner, inputs, required role, last-run)
Safe-runner executed worklets enforce RBAC checks against SSO groups and log an immutable audit event
Dry-run (--noop) available for all worklets and surfaced in UI with estimated changes
All worklets include automated smoke tests and a reviewable spec file in ops-worklets repo
Instrumentation: per-run metrics (duration, success, error-code) in Metrics dashboard and traces linked to run IDs
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with SRE + Support; aligned on 'worklet' naming to avoid runbook vs script confusion
2026-03-04: Decided to keep primitives language-agnostic; initial runner will support shell + Python adapters
2026-03-06: Prototype safe-runner accepts a declarative spec (YAML) that lists inputs, required_roles, and a dry-run snippet
2026-03-09: Security asked for HMAC-signed run artifacts and retention policy — added as requirement for audit logs
2026-03-11: Scoped MVP to 10 high-value worklets (rotate-keys, scale-down-dedicated-pool, refresh-kv-cache, revoke-session-tokens, collect-host-diagnostics)
comments: Marco Schmidt (2026-03-05): Pushed initial prototype to branch feature/worklet-runner. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-worklets/pull/78
Janelle Rivera - Security (2026-03-06): Requested threat model and storage plan for run artifacts; flagged that no plaintext secrets should be accepted as inputs
Priya Kulkarni - Support Lead (2026-03-08): Can we include an approval step for any worklet that impacts >1 customer? Suggest integration with Slack approvals channel
Design review (2026-03-10) by Ravi Chen: UI wireframes look fine; asked for clearer last-run error surface and link-to-run detail view
Marco Schmidt (2026-03-12): Demoed dry-run output in staging; discovered race condition when concurrent worklet executions target same resource — added locking to backlog
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement safe-runner core (RBAC checks, dry-run, telemetry) and seed 5 read-only worklets
Week 2: Add write-capable worklets behind internal feature flag and approval workflow
Week 3: Run a 2-week guinea-pig with SRE and Support; collect feedback and iterate
Week 4: Expand catalog to 10 worklets, finalize docs, and request security sign-off for GA
mitigation: All modifying worklets require an approval step and explicit justification logged
Inputs are schema-validated; secrets disallowed (use vault integration pattern)
Concurrent-run locking to avoid double-ops on same resource, fallbacks on conflict
Retention: run artifacts retained for 90 days and immutable once recorded
